The new `getOuterNormalDerivative` evaluates the Jacobian at the wrong corner of each patch.

In `gsBoundary.h:319-326`, `parameters_into` sets `param(i)` to 1 when the corner lies on the upper face in direction i (the end of the parameter range) and to 0 when it lies on the lower face. The new code does the opposite:

```cpp
pt(d,0) = parameters[d] ? supp(d,0) : supp(d,1);
```

It picks the lower bound `supp(d,0)` when the corner is on the upper end, and the upper bound when it is on the lower end. So for each corner it computes the Jacobian at the diagonally opposite corner of the parameter domain.

The cofactor-based normals for the boundary sides therefore come from the wrong point. On any patch that is not affine, they will be wrong. That affects the check for whether the two normals agree and the returned average normal, which the example then feeds into `normalsForPatches` and the corner collocation transforms. The fix is to swap the two branches: `parameters[d] ? supp(d,1) : supp(d,0)`.
